title: Castle moat liner with negative fixed charge around storage junction
idea: Random stimulus 'castle moat': a ring that repels attackers before they reach the wall. Line the isolation trench beside each storage-node junction with ALD Al2O3 carrying ~-5e12 cm^-2 fixed charge (borrowed from solar-cell field passivation), accumulating holes at the junction periphery and pinching the depletion region where trap-assisted and GIDL leakage live.
why: Periphery traps dominate the leakage tail; field passivation can cut tail leakage 3-10x (fact 3) with one ALD liner and no new masks.

title: Cookie-cutter procedural data regenerated from seeds instead of stored
idea: Like stamping cookies from a cutter instead of storing them, replace stored tensors that are pseudo-random or structured (random projections, initializations, LoRA bases, positional tables, dropout masks) with seeds plus near-memory generators. These recreate each line at access time.
why: Zero refresh: data that is never stored never needs refresh. It also cuts the DRAM footprint and data-movement energy (fact 5) for that share of memory.

title: Substitute electrical wordline with optical wordline and photoconductive access
idea: Substitute the metal wordline and gate with one silicon-nitride waveguide per row feeding a wide-gap (AlGaN or diamond) photoconductive switch at each cell. A pulse from an on-chip micro-LED makes the switch conduct; in the dark it is an insulator with attoampere-scale leakage.
why: Removes the 3 V wordline pump and the wordline RC delay and gives near-zero dark leakage (refresh-free retention); no wordline coupling for row hammer. Switching speed and persistent photoconductivity are the risk.

title: Substitute plasma etching of access pillars with TMAH crystallographic etch
idea: Substitute argon/helium-diluted plasma etch of fins and pillars with a hard-masked TMAH wet etch that stops on {111} planes. The channel sidewalls come out atomically flat and damage-free, with tightly controlled width.
why: Plasma damage and sidewall roughness create interface traps and Vt scatter; damage-free {111} sidewalls aim for ~3-5x lower interface-trap density, shrinking the leakage tail and VRT.

title: Ugly-produce program: sell retention-failing dies with in-system refresh grades
idea: Grocers turned misshapen fruit from waste into a discounted product line. Bin DRAM dies by measured retention (32/64/128/256 ms grades at 85 C) instead of scrapping those that miss 64 ms, and sell low-retention grades to hyperscalers whose controllers apply per-module refresh rates read from SPD.
why: Retention fallout is real yield loss at advanced nodes; recovering even 3-8% of dies adds bit supply without new fabs (capital intensity, supply).

title: Undoped channel with workfunction-set Vt shrinks the random-dopant tail
idea: A 12 nm access channel holds only ~50-100 dopant atoms, so Poisson fluctuation (sigma ~ sqrt(N)) gives sigma-Vt ~30-50 mV and a fat low-Vt tail. Remove channel doping and set Vt with a dipole-tuned workfunction metal (TiN with La or Al dipoles) in the buried wordline, as logic did with FinFETs. Sigma-Vt drops to ~10-15 mV, limited by metal grain granularity.
why: The refresh interval is set by the ~6-sigma cell. A 3x smaller sigma moves that cell ~150 mV closer to the median Vt, for ~100x less tail leakage and a 2-4x longer refresh interval using only logic's toolkit (fact 3).

title: District-metered well taps measure each subarray's real leakage
idea: Adapted from water districts that find leaks by metering minimum night flow per zone: give each subarray its own isolated p-well with a metered tap. During idle, an on-die current integrator reads the well current (where junction and GIDL leakage ends up), sets that subarray's refresh rate from the measurement, and flags sudden jumps caused by VRT or aging.
why: Replaces a global worst-case assumption with measured per-subarray leakage, letting cool, healthy subarrays refresh 2-8x less (fact 3) and catching variable-retention-time cells that one-time profiling misses.

title: Coal-mine canary cells that call for refresh only when needed
idea: Adapted from mining canaries and aviation condition-based maintenance: each subarray carries a few sentinel cells built with ~30% less storage capacitance and a longer gate-drain overlap, so they decay faster than the worst real cell. A tiny comparator polls them, and the bank is refreshed only when a sentinel crosses its threshold, not on a worst-case 32/64 ms timer.
why: Refresh is sized for the worst cell at the worst temperature; sentinels that track real temperature, voltage and aging let typical parts refresh 4-10x less often, cutting the 16-33% idle power and 10-20% bandwidth loss (fact 3).

title: Eliminate the worst-case guard band: deliberately leaky canary cells
idea: Embed a few sentinel cells per subarray built with intentionally shortened access transistors so they leak 4-8x faster than any real cell; a tiny comparator watches them and refreshes that subarray only when a canary crosses threshold. Refresh then tracks real temperature, voltage and aging instead of the 64 ms worst-case spec.
why: Most rows retain for seconds; replacing the fixed worst-case schedule with measured leakage cuts refresh operations 4-10x at typical temperatures, recovering most of the 16-33% idle-power share.

title: Quorum-sensing sentinel cells pace refresh per subarray
idea: Bacteria act only when autoinducer concentration passes a threshold; embed in each subarray five deliberately weakened sentinel cells (smaller capacitor, implanted to leak ~3 sigma worse than the real tail) with a local comparator, and refresh that subarray only when a quorum of 3 of 5 drops below threshold.
why: Refresh follows actual temperature, voltage and aging instead of worst-case 32/64 ms timers, so refreshes fall 3-8x in typical conditions and 10-20% of bandwidth comes back at 32-64 Gb.

title: Coral biomineral templating grows one crystal grain per access transistor
idea: Corals deposit amorphous calcium carbonate that crystallizes into oriented single crystals on an organic template; deposit amorphous In2O3/InGaO, place one ~10 nm crystalline seed per transistor site, and crystallize laterally at 300-350 C so every channel is a single grain with no boundary.
why: Grain boundaries drive the Vt and leakage tail in polycrystalline low-temperature oxides; single-grain channels could halve Vt sigma and cut tail leakage ~10x for uniform retention.

title: Insert NbO2 threshold switch to make access turn-on abrupt
idea: Substitute the plain access FET with a hyper-FET: a 10 nm NbO2 layer in series with the bitline-side source. NbO2's insulator-metal transition is at ~800 C, so it is stable at 85 C operation, and the layer snaps on abruptly once current flows, giving an effective sub-60 mV/dec turn-on. That lets the FET's Vt rise ~200 mV at the same wordline swing.
why: ~100x lower off-leakage from the higher Vt without raising VPP: longer refresh interval or a lower wordline voltage.

title: Magnify abruptness: NbO2 threshold switch in series (Hyper-FET)
idea: Insert a 10 nm NbO2 Mott threshold-switching layer between access transistor and storage node: below ~0.4 V it is insulating, cutting off-current 100-1000x, and when the wordline drives the cell above threshold it snaps metallic within ns. Its hysteresis window is tuned so stored '1' levels sit in the insulating regime.
why: Effective subthreshold swing <10 mV/dec cuts the leakage tail 100x+ without raising Vt; refresh ~10x rarer.

title: Seesaw cell plate lowers storage-node stress during standby
idea: Random stimulus 'seesaw': push one end down and the other end moves too. In idle mats the shared cell plate drops by ~0.3 V, coupling every storage node down with it; '1' nodes then sit lower against the negative wordline and well, cutting GIDL and junction fields, and the plate rises back just before activation.
why: GIDL depends exponentially on the drain-to-gate field; a 0.3 V standby shift can cut tail leakage several-fold and stretch refresh 2-4x (fact 3) using plate drivers that already exist.

title: Hand-warmer phase-change wax keeps HBM below the 85C refresh cliff
idea: Paraffin hand-warmers and chocolate tempering exploit a melting plateau to pin temperature. Pack a paraffin/graphite composite PCM melting at ~78 C into the HBM stack lid and mold cavity so burst workloads melt wax instead of pushing DRAM above 85 C, where JEDEC doubles the refresh rate.
why: Avoids the 2x refresh rate and its bandwidth loss during bursts (fact 3); paraffin is cheap and fluorine-free.

title: Reverse the airflow: DIMMs breathe first, processors second
idea: Rearrange server layout so cold inlet air, or the first segment of the liquid cold-plate loop, crosses the DRAM before the CPUs/GPUs: DIMM banks move to the chassis front and accelerators sit downstream. DRAM hot spots drop from ~85-95 C to ~50-60 C.
why: Exits the >85 C double-refresh range and halves leakage per ~10 C, so refresh energy and bandwidth loss fall ~2-8x (fact 3); a chassis change, no fab.

title: Minify transistors per bit: VCMA-gated spin-orbit strip with 8 MTJs
idea: Place 8 MTJs on one tungsten-free (Pt-alloy or BiSb) spin-orbit-torque write strip with a single access transistor; a voltage on each MTJ's top electrode lowers its anisotropy (VCMA) so only that MTJ flips when strip current passes, and reads use the same per-MTJ electrode.
why: One transistor per 8 bits, non-volatile, unlimited MTJ endurance, ns writes; ~3x SOT-MRAM density; sidesteps the tungsten chokepoint.

title: 200 K cool-not-cryo DRAM retargets Vt to cut wordline voltage
idea: At 200 K the Boltzmann limit falls from 60 to 40 mV/dec, and junction generation (Ea ~0.6 eV) is ~5e6 lower than at 85 C. Run memory sleds at 200 K with single-stage vapor-compression cooling. Spend the leakage windfall by lowering access-transistor Vt by about a third, so at equal Ioff wordline VPP drops from ~3 V to ~2 V and the array from ~1.1 V to ~0.8 V.
why: Refresh essentially disappears (fact 3), and CV^2 wordline and array energy falls ~45-55% (fact 10) after paying a cooling COP of ~0.6 at 200 K. The device is retargeted from first principles instead of run cold as-is.

title: Direct-tunneling charge-trap gate memory with seconds retention
idea: Po: the transistor remembers its own gate. Store the bit as electrons in a SiN trap layer above a 1.5-2 nm tunnel oxide; writes use direct tunneling at ~2 V in tens of ns with no hot carriers, so per-cycle damage is tiny, while retention is seconds rather than years, making a refresh-lite capacitorless DRAM.
why: Facts 1 and 3: no capacitor, and refresh 15x rarer than 64 ms; the risk is reaching 1e15 endurance.

title: Electret-microphone charge sets the access-transistor threshold permanently
idea: Adapted from electret microphones, whose fluoropolymer holds implanted charge for decades: implant a stable sheet of fixed charge into a deep-trap dielectric layer beside the access channel so its threshold is raised permanently, letting the wordline rest at 0 V instead of a negative voltage when off.
why: The negative off-wordline adds gate-drain field that drives GIDL and needs always-on charge pumps; an electret-set threshold keeps subthreshold leakage low while cutting GIDL and removing the negative pump's standby power (facts 3, 10).

title: Light is the wordline: photoconductor cells addressed by micro-LED rows
idea: Inverts 'the access device is a transistor on a metal wordline': a blanket wide-gap photoconductor film sits between capacitor dots and metal bitlines, insulating in the dark (retention set by very high dark resistivity), and a row is selected by flashing a stripe of a bonded micro-LED/waveguide array for ~10 ns. No transistors, no wordline drivers, two masks per layer.
why: Removes access transistors and much of the 49% periphery (fact 7) at film-coating cost, ~100x cheaper per GB; trade-off is optical power per access, 10-100 ns latency and photoconductor persistence.

title: Predictable decay: compensate unrefreshed analog weights instead of refreshing
idea: Inverts 'decay is an error to prevent': store neural-net weights as 4-6-bit analog charge in simple unrefreshed capacitor cells whose decay is a known exponential, and have the accelerator scale each tile's outputs by exp(+t/tau) using a per-tile timestamp and reference cell, reloading tiles from a NAND copy every few seconds.
why: No refresh circuitry plus 4-6 bits per cheap planar cell on mature nodes gives ~30-100x cheaper per GB for inference weights; trade-off is analog noise and per-cell tau spread.

title: Cleanroom-airlock double gate splits voltage across two stacked channels
idea: Put two independent gates on the same vertical pillar with a floating middle node, like a cleanroom airlock with two doors. In hold, the middle node settles mid-rail, so each channel sees half the Vds.
why: Subthreshold (DIBL) and GIDL leakage are exponential in Vds. The stack effect gives 10-100x lower off-current at zero added footprint in a vertical cell.

title: Eliminate the gate oxide: exfoliated beta-Ga2O3 Schottky-gate MESFET access
idea: Exfoliate or pattern beta-Ga2O3 nanomembranes and gate them directly with a Ni/Au Schottky gate, so there is no gate dielectric and no oxide or interface traps to cause random-telegraph leakage or variable retention time. The 4.8 eV gap gives aA-class off current.
why: Removes the trap-assisted tail behind refresh (fact 3); needs only e-beam lithography and evaporation; gallium avoids the W/He chokepoints.

title: Empty the channel: nano-vacuum field-emission access device
idea: Remove the semiconductor from the switch: the storage node faces a sharpened emitter tip across a sealed ~5-10 nm vacuum gap, and the wordline acts as an extraction gate. With the gate low there are no carriers in the gap, so leakage is only direct tunneling through vacuum; with the gate high, Fowler-Nordheim field emission conducts uA currents in picoseconds.
why: Access-device leakage (fact 3) essentially removed and retention no longer set by thermal generation, so refresh stops scaling with temperature; risks are emitter stability and gate voltage.

title: Zero-majority row encoding plus refresh skip for empty rows
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x SA with per-row invert flag and all-discharged flag x in-mat logic x Si x zero masks. Rows are written inverted when that leaves fewer charged (leak-vulnerable) cells, and rows flagged all-discharged are skipped by refresh since discharged true cells cannot decay.
why: Zero pages and sparse AI tensors are common; skipping them and halving charged cells elsewhere cuts refresh energy 20-50% and retention-failure exposure (fact 3).

title: Leak-aligned data encoding with standby bitline biasing
idea: IFR: every cell leaks toward the value it already holds. Each row gets an inversion flag chosen so most cells sit in the state their dominant leakage path (true-cell vs anti-cell) cannot corrupt, standby bitlines are held at the matching rail, and rows are refreshed by count of vulnerable cells only.
why: Fact 3: retention failures are mostly one-directional; aligning data to leak direction cuts cells needing refresh 50-80%, multiplying the effective refresh interval at zero process cost.

title: Pay at write, not at refresh: pre-emphasized writes for weak rows
idea: Reverse when weak cells are compensated: a per-bank retention map fused at test flags the ~0.1-1% weak rows, and whenever such a row is written or restored, the bitline restore level is boosted 150-250 mV for a few ns. The extra charge carries weak cells to the nominal interval instead of refreshing whole banks at the weak-cell rate.
why: Refresh rate is set by the tail (fact 3); boosting ~1% of rows lets the bulk period double (64 to 128+ ms) for <1% extra energy, with dielectric stress confined to a few rows.

title: Free-page hints stop refresh of unallocated rows
idea: Po: memory only remembers what someone cares about. The OS streams its free-page bitmap to the DRAM controller via a new mode-register/CXL command; rows whose pages are all free are dropped from the refresh rotation and are zero-initialized on next allocation.
why: Fact 3: servers often hold 20-50% free or clean-cache memory; skipping it cuts refresh energy and bandwidth tax proportionally.

title: LED constant-lumen drivers: aging-compensated negative wordline trim per mat
idea: Adapted from LED drivers that raise current as LEDs age to hold light output constant: each mat carries a replica access transistor whose leakage is measured monthly, and a small trim DAC deepens that mat's off-wordline voltage step by step to hold replica leakage at its day-one value, logging the trim history for refurbishers.
why: Compensates access-device aging in place (fact 3), so factory refresh settings stay valid over a 10-year life and second-life modules need no slower refresh.

title: Core-memory thermistor compensation: servo the off-wordline to leakage minimum
idea: Revive core memory's thermistor-compensated drive currents: a replica access transistor in each bank continuously measures total off-leakage (subthreshold plus GIDL), and a small dither loop holds the negative wordline voltage at the leakage minimum, which shifts with temperature and aging.
why: Fixed negative-wordline levels are set for the worst case and leave 3-10x leakage on the table across temperature (fact 3); tracking the minimum could double refresh intervals at hot corners.

title: Coincident-current selection: AND-gated access for column-selective refresh
idea: Revive core memory's coincident-current selection: each cell's access path has two series gates, one on the row wordline and one on a column-select line, so only the cell at the intersection opens. Refresh can then target only the few weak columns flagged at test, and reads stop overfetching whole pages.
why: Refresh energy scales with the number of weak cells rather than whole rows (fact 3), and the 128x overfetch disappears (fact 8): about 1.3x cell area for potentially 10x lower refresh energy.

title: Minify temperature to 77 K for pooled rack memory
idea: Put CXL-attached memory pools in a liquid-nitrogen dewar shelf: at 77 K subthreshold and generation leakage fall ~10^6x so retention reaches hours and refresh essentially stops, while lower wire resistance lets VARY drop to ~0.6 V. One cryocooler serves terabytes shared by a whole rack.
why: Removes refresh's 16-33% idle power and 10-20% bandwidth tax; CV^2 energy ~2.5x lower; cryo overhead amortized across the pool.

title: On-die telegraph-noise detector catches VRT cells in the field
idea: Effect: random telegraph noise from single-trap capture and emission. Inside idle REF windows each bank re-reads sample rows with a deliberately lowered sense reference; cells whose margin toggles (RTN signature) are logged in an on-die CAM and get extra internal refreshes while all other rows get fewer. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): catches cells that pass factory test then turn leaky, enabling safe 2-4x internal refresh relaxation.

title: Piano tuning: per-cell charge-trap trimming of leaky access transistor thresholds
idea: A piano tuner adjusts each string individually instead of rebuilding the piano. Add a thin LPCVD silicon-nitride charge-trap layer (dichlorosilane + ammonia, no fluorine) to the access gate stack; at wafer sort, find tail cells and apply hot-carrier program pulses through their own wordline and bitline to inject electrons and raise just their Vt by 150-300 mV.
why: A fluorine-free passivation flow leaves a slightly wider Vt tail; trimming the few-ppm worst cells collapses the leakage tail 10-100x (fact 3) so refresh is set by the median cell, not the outlier.

title: Capacitive-bootstrap wordline drivers retire the global VPP pump
idea: Effect: capacitive bootstrapping. Each wordline driver self-boosts: its gate node floats as the wordline rises and a coupling capacitor kicks it to ~2.8 V, so VPP is created locally from the transition rather than by a 30-40%-efficient global charge pump; timing fits normal ACT and REF. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Voltage floor and periphery (facts 10, 7): refresh energy -20-30% and pump area freed.

title: Bidirectional tunnel-FET pair sized to the 0.5 uA write budget
idea: Derive what the access device really needs: charging 5 fF by 1 V in 10 ns takes only I = CV/t ~0.5 uA, which a vertical GaSb/InAs or SiGe/Si heterojunction tunnel FET can supply. TFETs conduct in one direction, so stack two opposite-oriented vertical TFETs in one pillar, one for write and one for read. In the off state the band-to-band window is closed, with a sub-60 mV/dec slope.
why: This escapes thermionic Boltzmann leakage. Over a 0.6 V gate window, a 30 mV/dec average swing gives ~1e10 lower Ioff than a MOSFET at equal Ion, pushing retention from 64 ms to seconds or more (fact 3).

title: RV absorption fridge: GPU waste heat chills memory without fluorinated refrigerants
idea: Absorption refrigerators in RVs and hotels run on heat, using water/lithium-bromide or ammonia/water instead of HFC/HFO refrigerants. Drive a rack-level LiBr/water absorption chiller with the 60-90 C accelerator coolant return to make chilled water dedicated to HBM and DIMM cold plates at ~30 C.
why: Memory 30-40 C cooler cuts leakage ~8x and allows long refresh intervals (fact 3) using heat that is otherwise rejected, with no fluorinated refrigerant or PFAS immersion fluid.

title: Gateless rectifier access: ultra-wide-bandgap Schottky diode replaces the transistor
idea: Inverts 'the access device needs a gate': each capacitor reaches its bitline through a vertical Ga2O3 (4.8 eV) Schottky diode and the wordline is the cell plate; to write, raise the plate so the node clamps to the bitline level plus Vf, then drop it ('clamp-and-drop' sets any level), and to read, raise the plate and sense the dumped charge. Reverse leakage in a 4.8 eV material is orders of magnitude below silicon generation current.
why: Removes the 3-terminal transistor, its leakage tail (fact 3) and the 3 V boosted wordline (fact 10); a 2-terminal 4F2 cell stacks without a lateral transistor (fact 2).

title: Thin-film solar liquid-phase crystallization: monocrystal-grade silicon for stacked access tiers
idea: Thin-film solar groups melt silicon on glass with a scanning line-focus diode laser so it recrystallizes into centimeter-scale grains. Apply line-laser liquid-phase crystallization to each deposited amorphous-silicon tier of a 3D DRAM, seeded through windows opened in an alumina inter-tier dielectric with hot phosphoric acid, to get near-single-crystal lateral access channels without fluorinated etch or wafer bonding.
why: Grain-boundary traps make stacked poly-Si access transistors too leaky; LPC silicon could approach bulk leakage, the key blocker for 26+ tier 3D DRAM (facts 2, 3).

title: Pacemaker-style adiabatic refresh recycling charge between subarrays
idea: Implants live on nanowatts by never dumping charge to ground. During refresh, pair a subarray whose bitlines must rise with one whose bitlines must fall and move charge between them through a stepwise switched-capacitor ladder, so each refresh recovers roughly half of the bitline CV^2 instead of discarding it.
why: Fact 3: refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit) could drop ~40-60% and self-refresh standby power with it, for a few % more periphery area.

title: Magnetotactic self-alignment of single-crystal silicon nanowire access transistors
idea: Magnetotactic bacteria align along field lines via magnetosome chains; grow defect-free Si nanowires with gate-all-around shells at >900 C on a donor wafer, tip each with a Ni 'magnetosome' segment, release them into a fluid and pull them upright into pre-etched BEOL vias over the capacitor array with a magnetic field at room temperature, then contact them at low temperature.
why: Puts bulk-quality crystalline channels (~100x lower trap density than low-temperature films) into a <=400 C stack, giving FEOL-class fA retention in stackable DRAM tiers; placement yield is the risk.

title: Coulomb-blockade few-electron dot in axial nanowire heterostructure
idea: Po: the bit is ten electrons that cannot leave. Grow vertical nanowires with an axial Ge dot between two thin wide-gap barriers; Coulomb blockade plus band offset make adding or removing electrons a quantized step written by a gate pulse, and the dot charge gates the nanowire channel beneath it for readout.
why: Facts 1 and 3: one nanowire (~4F^2) per cell with no capacitor; barrier-set retention could reach seconds; speculative at room temperature.

title: Image-sensor black-reference rows let the sense threshold track decay
idea: Adapted from the optical-black reference pixels image sensors use to subtract dark current: every row stores a few reference cells written to 1 and 0 at the same moment as the data. On read, a charge-sharing averager builds the sense reference from those cells' decayed levels instead of a fixed VDD/2.
why: A fixed reference loses margin as stored 1s sag; a self-decaying reference keeps the decision point centered, roughly doubling usable retention and allowing 2x longer refresh intervals at the same error rate (fact 3) for ~1% area.

title: Delete the junction: dielectric-isolated junctionless storage node
idea: Inverts 'the storage node is a doped pn junction': build the access device as an accumulation-mode junctionless transistor in layer-transferred thin silicon on buried oxide, with the capacitor contacting a uniformly doped n+ segment wrapped in dielectric, so there is no depletion region where trap-assisted generation (the dominant tail mechanism) can occur.
why: Cuts the junction/GIDL-driven leakage tail (fact 3) 10-100x, pushing refresh toward seconds, and removes floating-body coupling that aids row hammer (fact 9).

title: Drown it in nitrogen: capacitorless tiers holding data for hours
idea: Inverts 'memory must work at room temperature': immerse memory sleds in liquid nitrogen, where subthreshold and generation leakage fall by many decades, so a bare gate-node or floating-body cell in many-tier poly-Si stacks with no capacitor at all retains for minutes to hours; LN2 at ~$0.1/L and cryo-rack designs carry the heat.
why: Deletes the capacitor module (fact 1) and allows cheap many-tier poly stacks with near-zero refresh, claimed ~100x cost/GB at NAND-like layer cost; trade-off is cryo plant energy and logistics.

title: Proton-intercalation transistor storing bits as channel conductance
idea: Po: the bit is a pH. Each cell is a three-terminal electrochemical transistor: a gate pulse pushes protons from a solid electrolyte (HfO2:H) into a MoO3 or SmNiO3 channel (avoiding the tungsten chokepoint), shifting its conductance; reading channel current is nondestructive and retention runs seconds to hours with no capacitor.
why: Facts 3 and 8: nondestructive read removes restore and overfetch penalties and long retention cuts refresh; risk is ns proton motion and endurance.

title: Capacitorless gain-cell memory tiles from mature U.S. logic fabs
idea: Po: memory made in a factory that has never made a capacitor. License a 3T silicon gain cell on 22-28 nm logic processes at existing U.S. foundries and sell it as memory tiles hybrid-bonded under accelerators, hiding its ~1 ms retention with retention-aware refresh, with no capacitor module, EUV or DRAM fab needed.
why: Fact 4 and capital: uses depreciated U.S. logic capacity (near-zero new capex) for near-compute buffers, offloading 10-20% of HBM demand.

title: Virtual cells: unpatterned film where fields, not etches, isolate bits
idea: Inverts 'each access transistor is a patterned island': deposit a blanket, unetched oxide-semiconductor film over crossing gate grids, and bias a 'fence' grid negative so it depletes the film around every crossing, electrostatically forming isolated storage pockets and access channels; each tier needs only metal-line masks, no active-area or channel etch.
why: Cuts per-tier masks 2-3x and removes etched channel edges that feed the leakage tail (fact 3); at 32+ tiers, claimed ~100x cheaper per GB; trade-off: fence bias power, isolation set by film quality.

title: Light is the wordline: photoconductive access switches on glass
idea: TRIZ #32 Changing optical properties: each cell's access switch is a high-dark-resistivity photoconductor (e.g., low-temperature-grown GaAs or amorphous-selenium-class film, >1e12 ohm-cm dark) on transparent glass, opened by a picosecond pulse from a row waveguide. Off leakage is set by dark conductivity, the optical wordline carries no CV2 charge, and wordline coupling disturbs vanish.
why: Removes the ~3 V wordline energy (Fact 10) and hammer coupling (Fact 9) with very low dark leakage for long retention (Fact 3); requires on-panel laser and waveguide integration.

title: Substitute blanket refresh with compiler-declared short-lifetime no-refresh zones
idea: Substitute uniform refresh with lifetime-aware refresh. An AI compiler places activations, gradients and KV-cache blocks that live shorter than the guaranteed retention window in banks flagged 'no-refresh', and the controller refreshes a bank only when its oldest live write exceeds that window. No new process or tool is needed, so no gases.
why: Much of accelerator DRAM holds data that lives under 10 ms; skipping its refresh cuts refresh energy ~50-80% in those banks and recovers bandwidth.

title: Scanning-tunneling-microscope gap switch: non-contact NEMS access device
idea: Adapted from the STM, whose current changes ~10x per angstrom of gap: a nano-cantilever tied to the storage node is pulled by the wordline from a 3 nm gap to ~0.8 nm from the bitline contact so electrons tunnel across in the on state. It never touches, so there is no contact wear, and at full gap tunneling current is ~1e-9 of on-current.
why: Removes the semiconductor junction from hold entirely, so off-leakage is set by vacuum tunneling (far below 1 aA) and retention could reach hours (fact 3); non-contact motion sidesteps the contact-wear endurance problem that stalled NEMS relays.

title: Static induction transistor revival as an oxide-free access switch
idea: Revive Nishizawa's 1950s static induction transistor: a vertical pillar whose current is pinched off by buried p+ junction gates, with no gate dielectric and no gate-drain overlap, so the off state is a pure electrostatic potential barrier. With no MOS overlap there is no gate-induced drain leakage and no oxide-trap-assisted tunnelling, the two mechanisms behind the DRAM tail.
why: Attacks the GIDL and trap-assisted tail (fact 3), with a claimed 10x tail reduction; junction gates swing ~1-1.5 V instead of a ~3 V wordline, so wordline CV2 drops 2-4x (fact 10).

title: Tunneling-only access switch: no thermal tail, attoamp off-state
idea: Inverts 'the access device is a thermionic MOSFET': replace it with a vertical heterojunction tunnel-FET (e.g., Ge/Si or GaSb/InAs source pocket) whose OFF current is set by band-to-band tunneling through a closed window rather than the Boltzmann tail. Orient it asymmetrically so the tunnel junction sits on the bitline side and the storage node only sees a wide-gap reverse junction.
why: Attacks the <=13 fA leakage tail (fact 3): subthreshold component falls toward aA, retention 64 ms -> >10 s, cutting refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit) and the 10-20% bandwidth tax by >90%; the TFET's low ON current is enough since a cell needs only ~0.5 uA (5 fF x 1 V / 10 ns).

title: Light-pumped self-restoring cell: photodiode gated by its own charge
idea: Box: cap x Si access nMOS x SA x backside-illuminated die under a uniform LED/laser sheet x thinned Si x BSI image-sensor process. Each cell adds a photodiode in series with a tiny transistor gated by the storage node, so a global light flash tops up only nodes that are already high, refreshing the whole array in parallel without any row activation.
why: Refresh energy/bandwidth (fact 3) moves from ~46 fJ/bit bitline CV2 to a few fJ/bit of photons with zero activations, also removing refresh-driven hammer (fact 9). Stray photocurrent into 0-nodes is the risk.

title: Silicon feedback-FET access switch borrows thyristor latch physics
idea: Scale jump from kilovolt power thyristors to a 15 nm vertical gated p-i-n: charge held in spacer-adjacent potential barriers creates positive feedback so the device turns on at <5 mV/decade, letting a 1 V wordline swing span ~10 decades between on and off current instead of ~6-7.
why: Leakage tail and voltage floor (facts 3, 10): deeper off-state for the same swing, wordline voltage from ~3 V to ~1.5 V, using Si, B, P and SiO2 only.

title: Persistent-current superconducting loops on sapphire for cryogenic racks
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transition: below Tc a superconducting loop's circulating current never decays, so retention is infinite. Patterned NbN or NbTiN nanowire loops on sapphire store a bit as clockwise or counter-clockwise flux, written and read through nanowire cryotrons (nTrons), giving byte-addressable cryogenic memory for superconducting logic and 4 K quantum-control systems.
why: Zero refresh and attojoule switching (Facts 3, 10); a niche (cryogenic computing) where DRAM fails outright, with ~1 um2 cells reachable; cooling cost limits scope.

title: Airlock isolation: a second hold gate that closes only in idle
idea: Inverts 'one access gate must serve both speed and isolation': split the vertical access pillar into a fast low-Vt segment driven by the wordline and an ultra-high-Vt 'hold' segment that is statically on during active periods and driven to about -1.5 V when a bank enters idle/self-refresh. The hold segment switches only on mode changes, so its slowness costs nothing.
why: Idle leakage drops 100-1000x (fact 3), cutting self-refresh power (16-33% of idle) by ~10x while active timing is unchanged; ~1 extra gate layer.

title: Deep-space soft-decision LDPC reading of decayed DRAM charge
idea: Adapted from the soft-decision LDPC decoding used by deep-space probes and 5G: a dual-threshold sense amplifier produces a 2-bit confidence value per cell before latching, and an on-die LDPC decoder over 512-bit codewords uses that soft information. Cells that have decayed near threshold are corrected rather than refreshed pre-emptively.
why: Soft decoding tolerates raw bit-error rates near 1e-3 versus ~1e-15 for hard reads, letting the refresh interval grow 8-16x (fact 3) and cutting refresh energy and bandwidth loss proportionally, for ~6% parity overhead.

title: Regenerative-braking refresh: recycle bitline and wordline charge
idea: Adapted from regenerative braking: when one subarray finishes restoring a refreshed row, its high bitlines are connected through charge-sharing switches to the next subarray's bitlines before discharging, and wordlines are driven by an LC resonant (adiabatic) driver that returns wordline charge to a tank instead of ground.
why: Refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit, fact 3) is mostly CV^2 from bitlines and the ~3 V wordline (fact 10); recovering half the bitline charge and most wordline charge could cut refresh energy 30-50%.

title: LPDDR partial-array self-refresh made real by OS compaction
idea: LPDDR has offered Partial Array Self-Refresh for years, but it went unused because OS allocators scatter live pages across every bank. Add a kernel 'refresh-aware compaction' pass that migrates live pages into the fewest banks before idle and marks the empty banks to the controller, which then stops refreshing them.
why: Claimed 50-80% cut in idle refresh power on phones, laptops and servers with partly free memory, with no hardware change.

title: Lazy refresh with LDPC resurrection across row groups
idea: Po: let bits die, then resurrect them. Refresh 8x less often and protect each group of 8 rows with a soft-decision LDPC code whose parity sits in a spare row; sense amps report a soft confidence level, and the decoder rewrites corrected data on read, treating decay as a noisy channel.
why: Fact 3: an 8x longer interval cuts refresh energy ~85% and returns 10-20% bandwidth for ~6% capacity overhead.

title: Silicatein biocatalytic silica liners grown near room temperature
idea: Sponges grow flawless silica spicules in cold seawater with the enzyme silicatein; tether silicatein-mimetic catalysts (imidazole/amine-terminated monolayers or peptides) to the sidewalls of high-AR access-channel and storage-node trenches, then expose to silicic acid or alkoxysilane vapor so dense SiO2 grows conformally only where the catalyst is, at <80 C.
why: Provides a hydrogen-poor, low-trap passivation and spacer around BEOL access devices without the 600-800 C oxidation and anneals, aimed at a 2-5x narrower leakage tail with conformality at AR >60:1.

title: Nitinol-stent style ferroelastic twin variants store bits as strain
idea: Borrow shape-memory-alloy training: a nanoscale ferroelastic or martensitic island is trained to two twin variants (strain orientations). A gate-adjacent piezo or electrostatic pulse flips it, and a piezoresistive channel underneath reads it.
why: Zero refresh: crystallographic twin state is non-volatile without charge storage. It differs from ferroelectric and MRAM routes and avoids leakage physics entirely.

title: Eliminate static storage: bistable Duffing MEMS resonators sustained by pump
idea: Each bit is the high- or low-amplitude branch of a nonlinear (Duffing) silicon-nitride nanomechanical resonator; one shared parametric pump tone keeps every resonator on whichever branch it occupies, so state is held by the pump, not by isolated charge. Writes kick a resonator between branches; reads sense amplitude capacitively.
why: Removes leakage-driven decay and per-row refresh (fact 3): retention is unlimited while the pump runs at ~aJ per resonator per cycle, from EUV-free SiN MEMS processing.

title: Check-valve cell: two opposing wide-bandgap diodes plus gain read
idea: Adapted from fluid check valves and the Tesla valve: the storage node is filled through one wide-bandgap diode from a 'fill' line and drained through a second, oppositely oriented diode to an 'empty' line. In hold, both lines park so both diodes are reverse-biased, and a read transistor gated by the storage node senses state without disturbing it.
why: Wide-bandgap heterojunction diodes (e.g., NiO/Ga2O3) can reverse-leak in the aA range, far below the 13 fA transistor tail (fact 3); thin-film diodes deposit above CMOS, which suits multi-tier 3D (fact 2).

title: Substitute mask lithography with solid-state DUV interference patterning
idea: Substitute neon-buffered excimer scanners with a frequency-quintupled solid-state laser (213 nm) in a two- or four-beam interference tool that prints the periodic wordline and active gratings without a mask; cut layers are done by imprint.
why: Interference gratings have near-zero CD variation and line-edge roughness, tightening access-transistor leakage spread, and remove the neon/EUV dependence at far below scanner cost.

title: Silver-catalyzed wet etching carves damage-free, ultra-high-aspect access trenches
idea: Ag: use metal-assisted chemical etching, in which a DUV- or block-copolymer-patterned Ag film sinks into silicon in HF/H2O2, cutting vertical trenches and pillars at >100:1 aspect ratio with no plasma, ion damage or charging, for buried-wordline recesses and vertical channels.
why: Plasma damage at the recess-gate sidewall seeds the traps behind GIDL and VRT tails (fact 3); a damage-free room-temperature wet etch could shrink the tail and cut etch-tool capital (fact 4).

title: Rack-level erasure coding lets DIMMs refresh ten times slower
idea: Scale jump from on-die ECC to cross-server parity: a CXL memory pool stripes each cache line plus parity across 10+2 memory nodes, each node refreshes only every ~0.5-1 s, and any decayed row is reconstructed from the other nodes and rewritten, so the rack, not the cell, guarantees retention.
why: Refresh energy at datacenter scale (fact 3): 8-16x fewer refreshes for ~20% parity overhead, plus reuse of retention-weak dies otherwise scrapped.

title: Metronome refresh locked to AI all-reduce phases
idea: Random stimulus 'metronome': everything happens on the beat. The accelerator tells HBM the beat of its training step, and the memory controller bunches all refresh into the predictable windows when HBM is idle (network all-reduce, optimizer step on cached data) instead of spreading it uniformly.
why: Hides most of the 10-20% refresh bandwidth tax (fact 3) without changing the cell; needs only system firmware plus a small refresh-postpone extension.

title: Diode-steered capacitor stack: one transistor, sixteen bits per pillar
idea: IFR: one switch serves a whole tower of bits. Deposit 16 plate-electrode/dielectric tiers around one vertical storage pillar, with a thin oxide Schottky diode in each tier between plate and capacitor, so a plate-line pulse forward-biases only the selected tier onto the shared pillar node, read through a single access transistor; tiers come from deposition and one hole etch.
why: Constraint: 16 bits per 4F^2 footprint is ~24x the bits of 6F^2 planar at ~1.5-2x wafer cost, about 10x bits per dollar; it also removes 15 of 16 access transistors and their leakage tail.

title: Optically gated wide-gap photoconductive access switches
idea: Worse: keep a gate field on a narrow-gap channel that leaks in the dark. Flip: replace wordline gates with GaN photoconductive switches lit by row-addressed micro-LED stripes; in the dark a wide-gap photoconductor holds essentially zero free carriers, so the off state is near-ideal.
why: Leakage (fact 3) potentially eliminated and wordline voltage floor (fact 10) bypassed.

title: Lead-free solder playbook: molybdenum oxychloride wordlines end WF6 fluorine damage
idea: Electronics went lead-free in a coordinated material swap that ended up improving reliability. Replace WF6-deposited tungsten buried wordlines with molybdenum from MoO2Cl2 on a TiCl4-based TiN liner, plus a low-workfunction n+ poly cap on the storage-junction side (dual-workfunction gate), so no fluorine diffuses into the gate oxide and storage-side GIDL drops.
why: Removes fluorine-induced oxide traps and cuts GIDL (fact 3) while dropping reliance on Chinese tungsten (~80%); Mo also has lower resistivity at narrow widths for faster wordlines.

title: Antiferroelectric capacitor that switches to nonvolatile mode for sleep
idea: Use a ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitor: high-k and non-remanent in DRAM mode. On sleep, a plate-line offset bias (as in work-function-engineered AFE memory) parks the loop so two polarization states hold with no power, and wake reads them back.
why: Removes self-refresh in standby (16-33% of idle power) and gives instant wake, while active-mode endurance stays unlimited.

title: Wordline bootstrap capacitor doubles as an analog hammer counter
idea: TRIZ #6 Universality: make an element already present in every row do a second job. Each local wordline driver gets a tiny MIM capacitor that receives a fixed charge packet on every activation (a switched-capacitor integrator) and is cleared on refresh; when it crosses a comparator threshold the driver flags its two neighbours for targeted refresh, giving exact per-row activation counting without SRAM counter tables.
why: Row hammer at ~1k activations (Fact 9) forces extra refresh: exact per-row analog counting replaces kilobits of counter SRAM and probabilistic schemes, cutting mitigation refreshes 5-10x with no coverage holes.

title: Over-center toggle-clamp NEMS relay isolates a junctionless MIM node
idea: The access device is a nano-relay with over-center (toggle-clamp) geometry: it latches open with no hold voltage and leaves a true air gap between bitline and a metal storage capacitor that has no pn junction.
why: Zero refresh: an open air gap conducts nothing, and with no junction only dielectric leakage remains (<1e-22 A), so charge persists for months or years. Contact wear is the honest risk.

title: OS-visible retention map steers long-lived pages to strong rows
idea: Worse: hide retention variation from software. Flip: the DIMM or CXL device reports per-region retention classes through a mailbox; the kernel puts page cache and cold heap in strong regions refreshed rarely and high-churn data in weak regions whose own write rate covers retention.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3) down 50%+ with no device change.

title: Replace semiconductor switch with non-touching tunneling-gap NEMS relay
idea: Substitute the channel with a vacuum-gap nanomechanical beam. When the wordline pulls it in, it stops ~1 nm from the storage electrode on an oxide standoff, so charge moves by electron tunneling and never by metal contact. When released (gap >5 nm), the only off-current is vacuum tunneling, effectively zero.
why: Leakage/refresh: off-leakage below an attoampere leaves retention limited only by the capacitor dielectric (hours). Because the contacts never touch, there is no wear (target >1e15 cycles).

title: FeRAM-style driven plate line biases cells during retention
idea: Segment the DRAM cell plate per subarray and drive it as FeRAM does. On entering standby, the plate steps so every storage node couples toward the bitline precharge level, which shrinks |Vds| and the junction field, and it steps back before the first ACT.
why: Subthreshold and junction or GIDL leakage are exponential in field and Vds, so self-refresh retention improves 2-5x. Idle power falls 10-20%.

title: Standby plate-line swing collapses storage-junction field during self-refresh
idea: Tail leakage is field-enhanced (trap-assisted tunneling ~ exp(gamma*sqrt(F))), so reduce the field instead of the conductance. On self-refresh entry, slowly ramp the shared cell plate down ~0.4 V. This couples every storage node down, so '1' cells sit closer to the p-well potential while '0' cells stay reverse-biased thanks to the negative p-well bias. Ramp the plate back before exit; its large capacitance is swung only twice per idle period.
why: A 0.4 V cut in junction reverse bias lowers field-enhanced tail current ~3-10x. That stretches self-refresh intervals by the same factor and cuts idle power 10-25% (fact 3).

title: Silicon-on-nothing void under every storage junction
idea: Box: cap x recessed access x SA x in-array x bulk Si with empty-space-in-silicon cavities x shallow trench array + high-temperature H2 anneal that migrates Si to seal a void beneath each storage diffusion. The junction bottom, usually the largest generation volume, now faces vacuum instead of depleted silicon.
why: Junction leakage (fact 3) cut 3-5x by area removal; lower junction capacitance also improves charge-transfer ratio.

title: Helium nanocavity gettering layer beneath every storage-node junction
idea: He: implant a low-dose helium layer ~200 nm below the buried-channel access transistors and anneal it into nanocavities whose inner surfaces chemisorb Fe, Cu, Ni and Au, so a gettering sink sits within diffusion range of every storage junction instead of at the wafer backside; the helium used is grams per fab-year, immune to the Qatar outage.
why: Metal deep levels drive the SRH generation behind junction-leakage tail cells (fact 3); proximity gettering could pull the tail in ~1 decade, giving 2-4x longer worst-cell retention.

title: Bias-only toolbox: co-pulse plate and well during idle
idea: Limit: no process change; only array biases may move. In long idle or self-refresh, ramp the cell plate and the array p-well down together by ~0.3-0.5 V. Every storage node then level-shifts down capacitively without forward-biasing its junction, which shrinks both the storage-to-wordline voltage that drives GIDL and the Vds of '1' cells. Both rails return before activation.
why: Facts 3 and 10: GIDL and junction leakage are exponential in field, so a 0.4 V shift could cut standby tail leakage ~5-10x. Standby is where refresh takes 16-33% of idle power.

title: Lightning-rod p+ electron drains between neighboring active regions
idea: Random stimulus 'lightning rod': give stray charge a better path to ground. Implant a narrow p+ stripe tied to the well under the passing wordline between neighboring active regions; electrons injected by aggressor wordline toggles recombine there before they can drift into the victim's storage node.
why: Attacks the charge-migration component of row hammer (fact 9) and the hammer-induced leakage that shortens retention; aims to raise the flip threshold from ~1k toward 10k+ activations and cut mitigation refreshes.

title: Ferroelectric domain-wall channel written only during row access
idea: Box: MIM cap x thin-film LiNbO3 where a conducting charged domain wall is nucleated between storage and bitline electrodes x SA x bonded-oxide tier x LNOI wafer x ion-slice bonding. Writing the wall opens a metallic path; erasing it leaves a ~4 eV insulator, so off-state leakage is that of bulk LiNbO3.
why: Wide-gap-insulator isolation pushes refresh toward zero (fact 3); LNOI wafers already come from US photonics lines. Wall nucleation speed and cycling endurance are the risk.

title: No fab, only an FPGA: per-row refresh via ACT/PRE
idea: 10-person constraint: we cannot touch the die, so we own the controller. An FPGA CXL memory expander profiles every row of commodity DDR5 at boot. It then replaces blanket auto-refresh with targeted ACT->PRE restores scheduled per row from a retention table: 64 ms for the weakest ~0.1%, 1-4 s for the rest, plus a VRT guardband.
why: Fact 3: 90%+ of refresh operations are spent on strong rows. This recovers most of the 10-20% refresh bandwidth and cuts refresh energy ~5-10x on unmodified DRAM, using only an FPGA board, firmware and a CXL IP license.

title: Carousel memory: rows stream past a reader, decoders deleted
idea: Inverts 'refresh is a background chore and random access needs decoders': read, regenerate and rewrite every row in a fixed cyclic order every ~1 ms using simple counters (no row/column decoders, no refresh controller), with a small SRAM front buffer catching requested rows as they pass; 1000 parallel carousels cut the wait to ~1 us.
why: Removes most of the 49% periphery (fact 7) and makes refresh the data path, so cells with 1000x worse leakage become usable; with relaxed-cell 3D builds, ~100x cost/GB for latency-tolerant bandwidth tiers.

title: Bit-plane split refresh: exponents guarded, low mantissa bits relaxed
idea: Bits do not carry equal information: a flipped low mantissa bit in bfloat16 perturbs a value by <2^-4 relative, while an exponent flip can be catastrophic. Transpose KV-cache and activation tensors into bit-planes. Sign, exponent and the top 3 mantissa bits go in normally refreshed banks; the low 4 mantissa bits go in banks refreshed 8-16x less. Validate on open LLMs with a ~$150k software and FPGA effort.
why: Relaxing refresh 8x on a quarter of KV-cache bits trims ~20% of its refresh energy with <6% error per value (fact 3).

title: BF16 split across refresh tiers: sign and exponent guarded, mantissa relaxed
idea: 10-person constraint: only data layout is ours. A custom allocator puts the sign-and-exponent byte planes of BF16/FP8 tensors in normally refreshed rows and the low mantissa bit-planes in rows refreshed every 1-2 s. It accepts rare low-order flips, which training and inference tolerate.
why: Fact 3: about half of tensor bits move to a ~20x slower refresh tier, cutting refresh energy ~45% for model memory with only an allocator and controller configuration.

title: Spindt molybdenum-cone vacuum access switch with zero channel leakage
idea: Revive SRI's 1968 Spindt molybdenum-cone field emitters and the vacuum triode: each cell's access device is a nanoscale vacuum gap with a tip made of Colorado-mined molybdenum and a gate ring. In the off state the vacuum holds no carriers, so leakage is only Fowler-Nordheim tunnelling, negligible at hold fields; build on 130-90 nm U.S. lines with wafer-level vacuum sealing.
why: Eliminates the leakage tail at the physics level (fact 3); molybdenum replaces China-sourced tungsten (resources), and no EUV is needed (fact 4).

title: Nanoelectromechanical relay access switch with air-gap zero leakage
idea: Po: the access transistor is always perfectly off. Replace the access FET with a vertical NEM relay whose cantilever is pulled onto the storage-node contact by the wordline field and springs back to leave a ~5 nm air gap, so off-state leakage is only gap tunneling (<1e-21 A); a low-adhesion RuO2 contact and pull-in/pull-out hysteresis keep the wordline swing under ~1 V.
why: Fact 3 leakage tail: removes subthreshold, GIDL and junction paths so retention is set by the capacitor dielectric alone; refresh interval could go from 64 ms to minutes (>1000x less refresh energy). Risk: 1e15-cycle contact endurance and ns mechanical switching.

title: EMP-hardened NEMS relay access switch with air-gap off-state
idea: Military and nuclear electronics use nanomechanical relays because radiation and EMP do not affect them. Build a vertical NEMS cantilever relay per cell that touches the storage-node contact only when the wordline pulls it in; off, an air gap gives zero subthreshold and junction leakage.
why: Fact 3: capacitor dielectric leakage becomes the only loss, giving near-static retention; risks are contact wear (>1e14 cycles needed in hot rows), stiction and 10-50 ns mechanical switching.

title: Piezoelectronic access switch with pressure-driven insulator-metal channel
idea: Effect: pressure-induced insulator-to-metal transition. A thin AlScN piezo actuator driven by the wordline squeezes a ~5 nm SmSe-class valence-change piezoresistor in series with the storage node; at ~1 GPa it turns metallic, and when unpressed it is a ~0.5 eV-gap insulator, so the hold path is a true insulator rather than a subthreshold channel.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): off-current set by a band gap, not the 60 mV/dec subthreshold slope; claims >100x lower leakage, refresh interval from 64 ms to seconds, and refresh's 16-33% idle power falls to ~1%.

title: Atomically thin junctionless sulfide access switch with no p-n junction
idea: S: make the access device a uniformly doped bilayer SnS2 or MoS2 ribbon with no source/drain junctions; the ~1.3 nm body is fully depleted by the gate in the off state, so there is no junction volume for SRH generation and no drain-overlap region for band-to-band tunnelling.
why: Removes both junction leakage and GIDL (fact 3), the two dominant tail mechanisms of recessed silicon access transistors; off-current is limited to thermionic emission over a 1.5-2 eV barrier.

title: Optically gated access: waveguide wordlines, zero-dark-current channel
idea: IFR: a switch with no electric gate to leak through. Use an ultrawide-gap photoconductive channel (AlN or Ga2O3, negligible dark current) as the access device, and route each wordline as a silicon-nitride waveguide that delivers a ~1 ns UV pulse to open a whole row of channels.
why: Fact 3 and 10: dark leakage at 4.8-6 eV is essentially nil so refresh nearly vanishes, and wordline CV^2 becomes photon energy; waveguide pitch versus cell pitch is the density risk.

title: Frequency-addressed resonant access: 64 cells share one wire
idea: IFR: address a cell with no wire of its own. Each of 64 cells on a shared line gets a nanomechanical resonator switch with a unique resonant frequency (set by beam length in one patterning step); an RF burst at f_k makes only cell k's beam swing into contact and connect its capacitor, cutting wordline and decoder count 64x.
why: Constraint: wordlines, drivers and decoders are much of the area (fact 7, periphery ~49%); frequency multiplexing over a passive array targets ~10x density at similar cost, with zero off-leakage across open gaps.

title: Wafer-reclaim Smart Cut: reusable donor wafer gives SOI access transistors
idea: Adapted from SOI layer transfer and the wafer-reclaim trade: cleave a thin single-crystal layer for the access transistors off a donor wafer by hydrogen implant, bond it onto oxide on the carrier, then repolish and reuse the donor 10+ times; the buried oxide removes the storage-junction-to-substrate leakage path.
why: Junction-to-substrate leakage is a main tail component (fact 3) and SOI removes it; donor reuse cuts consumption of CZ wafers grown in Spruce Pine quartz crucibles (resource chokepoint).

title: Tear-off notepad: reusable donor wafer for transferred access layers
idea: Random stimulus 'tear-off notepad': many sheets from one block. Form the single-crystal silicon access-transistor layer by repeated hydrogen-split layer transfer from one thick donor wafer (10-20 transfers per donor, plasma touch-up between splits) onto a capacitor-first array wafer, instead of consuming a fresh polished prime wafer as the access substrate.
why: Prime-wafer making (CZ growth in Spruce Pine quartz, slicing, lapping, polishing, cleaning) carries large embedded water; reusing the donor cuts substrate-attributable water per access layer >10x and enables capacitor-first stacking toward 3D (facts 2, 3).

title: Veneer-peeled single-crystal foils give every 3D tier bulk-grade transistors
idea: Like a rotary veneer lathe peeling a log, repeatedly cleave 30-50 nm single-crystal Si foils from one reusable donor boule (H-implant plus stressor-controlled spalling) and bond them tier by tier, so each of 26+ tiers gets bulk-quality lateral access transistors with no Si/SiGe superlattice epi and no poly-Si.
why: Fact 2 (lateral transistor blocker): single-crystal channels avoid poly grain-boundary leakage (~100x lower tail) in every tier, and donor reuse keeps cost per tier to a bond plus cleave step.

title: Eliminate the three-terminal transistor: threshold-switch selector 1S1C crosspoint DRAM
idea: Isolate each capacitor with a two-terminal volatile threshold switch (OTS or NbO2 Mott selector) stacked directly on it in a crosspoint, addressed by V/2 biasing; no wordline transistor and no lateral device, so tiers stack like 3D crosspoint.
why: Removes the 3D DRAM lateral-transistor blocker (fact 2) and enables 4F^2 stacking; half-select leakage must reach <1e-15 A for even millisecond retention, hence high risk.

title: Solar-industry kerfless epitaxial wafers: no quartz crucible needed
idea: Solar makers grow wafers directly on porous-silicon templates and lift them off, with no crucible. Use kerfless epitaxial or UMG-seeded substrates with heavy gettering for DRAM array wafers, accepting ~10x shorter carrier lifetime and higher junction generation leakage as errors inside the 1% budget.
why: Resources: removes high-purity quartz crucibles (Spruce Pine >80%) and much CZ crystal capacity from array wafers; substrate cost could fall ~2-3x.

title: Electrolytic-capacitor anodizing: alumina pore templates grow vertical access channels
idea: Aluminum electrolytic-capacitor makers anodize foil in oxalic or phosphoric acid, self-organizing billions of straight nanopores. Anodize a deposited aluminum film over the array (pitch 25-40 nm set by anodizing voltage), thin the pore-bottom barrier in phosphoric acid, then fill pores bottom-up with selective epitaxial silicon to form gate-all-around vertical access channels, with no fluorocarbon high-aspect-ratio etch anywhere.
why: Mask-free, self-assembled 4F2-class access pillars (facts 2, 4) with all-around gates for low leakage; replaces an EUV-patterned pillar etch with a wet bath.

title: Sourdough-starter replica cells clock each mat's refresh
idea: Random stimulus 'sourdough starter': you feed it when it looks hungry, not on a fixed clock. Each mat holds 64 deliberately weakened replica cells (shorter gate, thinner spacer) written high at every refresh; a comparator fires that mat's refresh only when the median replica sags past threshold, so the interval tracks real temperature, aging and process instead of a worst-case 64 ms at 85 C.
why: Most mats retain for seconds; replica-gated refresh cuts refresh operations and their 16-33% idle-power share by ~70-90% while the deliberately weaker replicas guarantee coverage (fact 3).

title: Refresh commands rationed to zero: per-row canary cells call refresh
idea: Limit: the controller may issue no periodic refresh. Each row carries 2 deliberately weakened replica cells (thinner capacitor, longer drain overlap) that always hold '1' and feed a tiny comparator on the local sense line. When a canary decays past threshold, the row raises a flag and is restored. Refresh becomes event-driven and tracks real temperature and VRT.
why: Fact 3: most rows retain data for seconds, so restoring only when a canary trips could cut refresh operations ~10-50x versus 64 ms worst-case scheduling and removes temperature guardbands.

title: HPE memristor sneak paths cured by self-closing diffusive access
idea: HPE's TiO2 memristor crossbars died on sneak currents because they had no selector. Turn that failure around with an Ag-doped SiO2 diffusive memristor: it grows a filament only while a wordline pulse is applied, and the filament dissolves by itself within ~0.1-1 us. Used as a two-terminal volatile access switch in series with a stacked MIM capacitor, it gives >1e10 on/off with sub-fA off-current.
why: A two-terminal 4F2 access device that can be stacked in BEOL tiers, enabling 3D DRAM with no lateral transistor. Off-leakage far below the 13 fA tail cuts refresh 10-100x.
